messages:
alex: heads-up — mypy started failing on the sampleapp e2e pipeline after the autogen model stubs change. CI error looks like a circular import in the TypedDicts. repro below.

alex: minimal repro (autogen creates these two files):
```py
# models/user.py (autogen)
from typing import TypedDict
from .account import AccountDict

class UserDict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    account: AccountDict

# models/account.py (autogen)
from typing import TypedDict
from .user import UserDict

class AccountDict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    owner: UserDict
```

alex: mypy output: `error: Cannot determine type of "models.user.UserDict"` and points to the circular import. pyright also flags unresolved import in CI.

maria: ugh — classic. two quick options: use `from __future__ import annotations` + stringified forward refs, or emit the stubs as `TypedDict` with `typing.TYPE_CHECKING` guarded imports.

sam: did you try `from __future__ import annotations`? that usually fixes forward ref evaluation for typing-only references.

alex: i added `from __future__ import annotations` to both stubs locally and mypy stopped complaining. but pyright in the repo still errors in the lsp step (it doesn't fully honor future annotations in all cases).

ingrid: we should probably make the autogen opt-in: generator flag `--use-future-annotations` and default to on for py3.10+. also consider generating `if TYPE_CHECKING: from .user import UserDict` and keep runtime imports minimal.

maria: +1 to `if TYPE_CHECKING`. that's what we've used for circular model refs in other places. also emitting `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING` in stubs is safe.

sam: small nit — our sampleapp uses `from models import User` imports in runtime code which breaks if stubs-only changes rely on TYPE_CHECKING. need to make sure runtime package has concrete classes or keep runtime imports intact.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapp/mypy e2e failed — https://ci.internal/1234/build/5678 (mypy error) :eyes:

alex: plan: i'll open a generator PR to emit `from __future__ import annotations` at top of stubs + add TYPE_CHECKING guards for inter-model imports. will add a toggle flag so downstreams can opt-out.

ingrid: can you also add a small mypy/pyright test in generator repo that compiles the generated stubs against a circular-model example? that'll catch regressions.

alex: yes, adding tests. quick workaround for the sampleapp repo: pin generator to previous release or patch the local stubs with future import until PR lands.

maria: FYI pyright team suggested using `"pythonVersion": "3.11"` in pyrightconfig to be more permissive with annotations — might help some users.

sam: one more edge: async context managers in some autogen clients annotate `__aenter__` return types with generated models, which reintroduces import cycles at runtime. we should prefer `-> Any` on dunder async methods or use string forward refs.

alex: noted — i'll include a follow-up to avoid strong typed return on magic methods and prefer `Any` for now (keeps DX better and avoids cycles).

ingrid: thanks — that should keep CI green. please tag me on the PR and i can help with the test harness. :+1:

alex: will do. opening PR in 30m. link when ready.

maria: thanks team.
